sections.title: Introduction
sections.text:
In Arcs, you lead a spacefaring society through an epic saga, as you try to survive in the harsh and dangerous Reach at the galaxy's edge. A game of Arcs lasts until someone has enough **Power**—essentially points. In games with 4 players, someone needs to have at least **27 Power**. With 3 players, **30 Power**. With 2 players, **33 Power**. When the game ends, the player with the most Power wins.

You gain Power by completing **ambitions**, which are objectives that you declare in play. These are scored at the end of the **chapter**, when everyone runs out of action cards. The game lasts a varying number of chapters, usually three to five.

Your first game of Arcs will take about 45 minutes per player. After you play a few times, a game should take about 30 minutes per player.

If you want to learn Arcs by watching a video, click **[here](https://buriedgiantstudios.com/pages/how-to-play-arcs)**.

sections.title: Map
sections.text: The map of the Reach is where the action happens. You can move your ships around it, battle Rivals for control over its systems, and tax resources from the cities you build on its planets.

sections.title: Player Pieces
sections.text: Each player has the following pieces. The box contains pieces for 4 players.

sections.title: Player Board
sections.text: This board holds resources, your unbuilt cities, and Rival pieces you take as Trophies and Captives.

sections.title: Starports
sections.text: Starports are built on planets and are used to build ships. Each player has **5 starports**.

sections.title: Cities
sections.text: Cities are built on planets and can be taxed to gain resource tokens onto your player board. Each player has **5 cities**.

sections.title: Ships
sections.text: Ships can move around the map and engage in battles. Each player has **15 ships**.

sections.title: Agents
sections.text: Agents are placed on cards in the Court, a card row next to the map. Once you have the most agents on a card in the Court, you can take it. Each player has **10 agents**.

sections.title: Power Marker
sections.text: This marker tracks your current Power on the bottom map edge. The second marker is used in expansions to track negative Power and very high Power. Each player has **2 power markers**.

sections.title: Objective Marker
sections.text: This shows how close you are to completing your Fate's objective.

sections.title: Flagship Piece
sections.text: Some Fates turn you into a Flagship, adding this piece to the map.

sections.title: Flagship Board
sections.text: Some Fates turn you into a Flagship, giving you this board.

sections.title: Action
sections.text: These cards are played to take actions and declare ambitions. With 2 or 3 players, you don't use the “1” and “7” action cards. There are **28 action cards**.

sections.title: Setup
sections.text: One of these cards is used in setup to place players' starting pieces and cover parts of the map. There are **12 setup cards**, 4 each for 2-4 players.

sections.title: Leader
sections.text: These cards give special powers and show a player's starting pieces and resources. They are used in Leaders & Lore mode (`rule-relative:Leaders & Lore`). There are **8 leader cards** in the base game and **8 leader cards** in the Leaders & Lore pack.

sections.title: Guild
sections.text: These cards represent the support of guildmasters and task forces. They are gained from the Court, often give new actions, and can be stolen.

sections.title: Base Game
sections.text: There are **25 Guild cards** for the base game, marked “BC” in their bottom-left corner.

sections.title: Campaign
sections.text: There are **10 Guild cards** for the campaign game, marked “CC” in their bottom-left corner.

sections.title: Vox
sections.text: These cards represent incidents in the Reach that you can turn to your own ends. They are gained from the Court and resolve immediately.

sections.title: Base Game
sections.text: There are **6 Vox cards** for the base game, marked “BC” in their bottom-left corner.

sections.title: Campaign
sections.text: There are **5 Vox cards** for the campaign game, marked “CC” in their bottom-left corner.

sections.title: Lore
sections.text: These cards represent long-lost technologies and the intangible qualities of leadership, charm, and rank. They are used in Leaders & Lore mode (`rule-relative:Leaders & Lore`). There are 14 lore cards in the base game and 14 lore cards in the Leaders & Lore pack.

sections.title: Event
sections.text: Two or three of these new action cards are added to the action deck during campaign setup. There are **3 Event cards**.

sections.title: Imperial Council
sections.text: This new card in the Court during campaign lets players take advantage of Imperial politics. It is marked `symbol:diamond`01.

sections.title: Edict
sections.text: These are put in the rules booklet and may resolve during events. They are marked `symbol:diamond`02–05. There are **4 Edict cards**.

sections.title: Regent/Outlaw Title
sections.text: In the campaign, every player starts as an Imperial Regent and might become an Outlaw. They are marked `symbol:diamond`06–09. There are **4 Regent/Outlaw Title cards**.

sections.title: Flagship Upgrades (4)
sections.text: These aid cards give the rules for Flagship Upgrades, marked `symbol:diamond`10–13. There are **4 Flagship Upgrades cards**.

sections.title: Cards
sections.text: These tarot-size cards show your Fate, which can change over time. There are **24 Fate cards**, 8 each of A, B, and C.

sections.title: Sets
sections.text: Each Fate has a set of many cards and pieces you will use in play.

sections.title: Set Dividers
sections.text: Each Fate Set is stored behind the divider of matching number.

sections.title: Resource Tokens
sections.text: Resources represent both assets and the people skilled in using them. They add to ambitions and can be spent for special actions. There are **25 resource tokens**, 5 each of Material, Fuel, Weapons, Relics, and Psionic.

sections.title: Battle Dice
sections.text: These dice are used to resolve battle. There are **18 battle dice**, 6 each of Assault, Skirmish, and Raid.

sections.title: Chapter Marker
sections.text: This marker tracks the current chapter of the game on the map.

sections.title: Ambition Markers
sections.text: These markers show which ambitions are currently declared. They start on their blue side with lower numbers. There are **3 ambition markers**.

sections.title: Zero Marker
sections.text: This marker covers the card number of the lead card, making it 0, when an ambition is declared.

sections.title: Initiative Marker
sections.text: This marker shows which player will take the first turn of a round.

sections.title: Path Markers
sections.text: These are added to the map during setup. They cover gates, making them out of play and connecting the gates of neighboring clusters. There are **4 path markers**, 2 each of long and short.

sections.title: Out-of-play Markers
sections.text: These are added to the map during setup. They cover planets, making them out of play for the game. There are **6 out-of-play markers**.

sections.title: Blight Tokens
sections.text: The Blight is a mysterious entity spreading through the Reach. There are **24 Blight tokens**.

sections.title: Free Cities & Starports
sections.text: Players can act with Free buildings they control. There are **28 Free cities** and **14 Free starports**.

sections.title: Imperial Ships
sections.text: These ships control systems for the Empire, and Regents can act with them. There are **15 Imperial ships**.

sections.title: Number & Event Dice
sections.text: These are rolled in setup and during some events in play.

sections.title: Chapter Track Tile
sections.text: This double-sided tile covers the chapter track on the map.

sections.title: First Regent Tile
sections.text: This shows which Regent is the First Regent and holds the Imperial Trust.

sections.title: Rules Booklet
sections.text: This booklet holds various cards that are added in play.

sections.title: Overflow Markers
sections.text: These hold pieces from crowded parts of the map between sessions. There are **4 overflow markers**.

sections.title: Other Dividers
sections.text: You can store cards and pieces behind these dividers (`rule-relative:Intermission$Next Act?$Next Act.$Packing Up.`). There are **6 other dividers**.

sections.title: Base Game
sections.text: These sheets summarize how to play and what actions you can take. There are **4 aid sheets** for the base game.

sections.title: Campaign
sections.text: These aids give rules for campaign play, ending games, and setting up later games. There are **2 aid sheets** for the campaign.

sections.title: Log Sheet Pad
sections.text: These sheets record players' details between games.

sections.title: Base Game
sections.text: If you are starting a non-campaign game, use this section. This section assumes that  you are not using Leaders & Lore (`rule-relative:Leaders & Lore$Setup`).

sections.title: Map, Dice, and Tokens
sections.text: Place the map and collect the 18 battle dice and 25 resource tokens.

sections.title: Initiative Marker
sections.text: Give the initiative marker to a random player.

sections.title: Action Deck
sections.text: Shuffle the 20 action cards marked "2" through "6" to start the action deck.

sections.title: Action Deck (4 Players Only)
sections.text: Shuffle the 8 action cards marked "1" and "7" into the action deck. (Otherwise, return them to the box.)

sections.title: Ambition Markers
sections.text: Place the 3 ambition markers on their blue, lower-numbered sides in the Available Markers section of the map.

sections.title: Chapter Marker
sections.text: Place the chapter marker on the "1" space of the Chapter track on the map.

sections.title: Zero Marker
sections.text: Place the zero marker in the Ambition Declared slot on the map.

sections.title: Court Deck and Row
sections.text: Shuffle all 6 Vox and 25 Guild cards to make the Court deck. Draw **3 cards (2 players)** or **4 cards (3–4 players)** from this deck to make a face-up Court row.

sections.title: Setup Card
sections.text: Shuffle the setup cards that list your number of players. Draw 1 setup card.

sections.title: Path and Out-of-Play Markers
sections.text: In the **2 clusters (2–3 players)** or **1 cluster (4 players)** on the map marked Out of Play on the setup card, place a path marker over its numbered gate and place 3 out-of-play markers over the planets touching that gate.

sections.title: Resources on Ambitions (2 Players Only)
sections.text:
Place the 6 resource tokens matching the 6 planets covered by out-of-play markers onto the ambition boxes:
\- Material and Fuel go on Tycoon.
\- Weapons go on Warlord.
\- Relics go on Keeper.
\- Psionics go on Empath.

sections.title: Player Pieces
sections.text: Each player chooses a color, collects the matching player board, 5 cities, 5 starports, 15 ships, and 10 agents, and places the cities in the triangle slots along the top of their player board.

sections.title: Power Marker
sections.text: Each player puts their Power marker on the "0" Power track space on the map.

sections.title: Starting Placement
sections.text:
Players simultaneously place their starting pieces onto the map as follows. The player with the initiative marker performs the following steps. Then, going clockwise from the player with initiative, the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th players set up in the same way in the systems marked 2A–C, 3A–C, and 4A–C on the setup card, respectively.
\- Place **3 ships and 1 city** in the system marked 1A on the setup card. Place the leftmost city from your player board.
\- Place **3 ships and 1 starport** in the system marked 1B.
\- Place **2 ships** in the system (3–4 players) or 2 systems (2 players) marked 1C.

sections.title: Starting Resources
sections.text: Each player gains the 2 resource tokens matching the planet icons in their A and B systems, putting them in the leftmost and next leftmost circle slots on their player board, respectively.

sections.title: Starting Hand
sections.text:
Each player draws 6 action cards into their hand.
***2 Players Only:*** The player without initiative may discard all 6 action cards in their hand and draw 6 new ones.

sections.title: Action Discard Pile
sections.text: Discard all action cards not in players' hands into a facedown action discard pile on the map, then shuffle it.

sections.title: Campaign (Act I)
sections.text:
If you are starting a campaign from the beginning, use this section. Otherwise, use Act II & III Setup (`rule:3.2`). Campaign setup is very different from single session setup. Here are the important changes:

  - Do not use setup cards. No clusters will be out of play, and players place
    their starting pieces differently.
  - Use the Guild and Vox cards specific to the campaign Court (marked "CC"). Do
    not use the cards for the base Court (marked "BC").
  - Use the same deck of lore cards as the base game (marked "L"), but you will
    shuffle lore into the Court deck after dealing the Court.

sections.title: Map, Dice, Tokens, and Free Pieces
sections.text: Place the map on the table and collect the 18 battle dice, 25 resource tokens, 24 Blight tokens, 28 Free cities, and 14 Free starports.

sections.title: Initiative Marker
sections.text: Give the initiative marker to a random player.

sections.title: Action Deck
sections.text: Shuffle the 20 action cards marked "2" through "6" to start the action deck.

sections.title: Action Deck (4 Players Only)
sections.text: Shuffle the 8 action cards marked "1" and "7" into the action deck.

sections.title: Event Cards
sections.text: Shuffle 2 Event action cards (2–3 players) or 3 Event action cards (4 players) into the action deck.

sections.title: Ambition Markers
sections.text: Place the 3 ambition markers on their blue, lower-numbered sides in the Available Markers section of the map.

sections.title: Chapter Track Tile and Marker
sections.text: Place the Chapter track tile to cover the chapter track on the map, with its "Act I & II" side face up, and place the chapter marker on its "1" space.

sections.title: Zero Marker
sections.text: Place the zero marker in the Ambition Declared slot on the map.

sections.title: Court Deck and Row
sections.text: Shuffle all 15 campaign Vox and Guild cards (marked "CC") to make the Court deck. Deal 3 cards (2 players) or 4 cards (3–4 players) from it into the Court row.

sections.title: Lore Cards
sections.text: Shuffle 1 lore card per player at random from the lore deck into the Court deck. _Use the same lore deck as you use in the base game. You can add any lore cards you want from expansion packs._

sections.title: Imperial Council Card
sections.text: Place the Imperial Council card (`symbol:diamond`01) on its In Session side as the leftmost Court card.

sections.title: Guild Envoys Depart (2 Players Only)
sections.text: Slide the Guild Envoys Depart edict card (`symbol:diamond`02) into the first slot in the rules booklet.

sections.title: Govern Edict Cards
sections.text: Shuffle the 3 Govern the Imperial Reach edict cards (`symbol:diamond`03–05) face down, flip them all over, and slide them all face up into the first available slot in the rules booklet.

sections.title: Imperial Ships
sections.text: Roll the number die, then set up the 2 Imperial clusters—in the rolled cluster and the next clockwise cluster, place 1 Imperial ship in each system. _(8 total.)_

sections.title: Free Cities
sections.text: Roll the event die. Place 1 Free city on each planet of the rolled planet ID symbol outside the Imperial clusters.

sections.title: Damaged Blight
sections.text: Place 1 damaged Blight _(shaded side)_ in each system outside the Imperial clusters.

sections.title: Resources on Ambitions (2 Players Only)
sections.text:
Place the 6 resource tokens matching the planets in Imperial clusters onto the ambition boxes:
\- Material and Fuel go on Tycoon.
\- Weapons go on Warlord.
\- Relics go on Keeper.
\- Psionics go on Empath.

sections.title: Player Pieces
sections.text: Each player chooses a color, collects the player board, 15 ships, 5 cities, 5 starports, and 10 agents of that color, and places those cities in the 5 triangle slots along the top of their player board.

sections.title: Fate Cards and Sets
sections.text: Each player draws 2 "A" Fate cards ("A" on card back) and chooses one secretly. After everyone chooses, reveal them and take the matching Fate Sets (`rule-relative:What's in the Box$Fates`).

sections.title: Objective Card Setup
sections.text: Each player sets up based on the Setup side of their objective card—the first card in their Fate Set—then flips the card to its Objective side.

sections.title: Objective Marker
sections.text: Each player places their objective marker on the Power track space shown by the large clock on their objective card.

sections.title: Power Marker
sections.text: Each player puts their Power marker on the "0" Power track space on the map.

sections.title: Regent/Outlaw Title Card
sections.text: Each player takes a Regent/Outlaw title card (`symbol:diamond`06–09) and tucks it partially under their Fate card with its Regent side up. If no one has the First Regent tile from their setup, the player with initiative takes it.

sections.title: First Placement
sections.text: In turn order, each player places 3 ships and 1 building in an empty building slot at a planet with an Imperial ship and gains 1 resource token of that planet type. _(The planet can have Rival pieces.)_

sections.title: Second Placement
sections.text: Repeat the previous step but in reverse turn order—start with the last player in turn order and go counterclockwise.

sections.title: Remaining Free Cities
sections.text: Place Free cities in all empty building slots on planets with Imperial ships. _(With 4 players, you might not place any.)_

sections.title: Starting Hand
sections.text:
Each player draws 6 action cards into their hand.
***2 Players Only:*** The player without initiative may discard all of the action cards in their hand except Events and draw the same number of new cards from the action deck.

sections.title: Action Discard Pile
sections.text: Discard all action cards not in players' hands into the action discard pile on the map.

sections.title: Campaign (Act II & III)
sections.text: Set up Act II or III so it's the same as the previous Act, including Power, with these changes:

sections.title: Ambition Markers
sections.text: In Act II, flip the lowest-Power ambition marker to its higher-Power side. In Act III, flip the two lowest-Power ones to their higher-Power sides. The others start on their lower-Power sides.

sections.title: Court Deck and Imperial Council
sections.text: Shuffle the Court deck and deal 3 cards (2 players) or 4 cards (3–4 players) from it into the Court. Flip the Imperial Council card to In Session.

sections.title: Blight on Gates
sections.text: Place 1 damaged Blight on each gate that has no Blight and no ships.

sections.title: Blight on Planets
sections.text: Roll the event die. In each cluster, place 1 damaged Blight at the planet with the rolled ID symbol if it has no Blight. If it does have Blight, place 1 damaged Blight at each planet in its cluster with no Blight.

sections.title: Resources on Ambitions (2 Players Only)
sections.text: Roll the number die twice. Place the 6 resource tokens matching the planets in the 2 rolled clusters onto ambition boxes as in `rule:3.2.1.17`. _(If the resource supply empties, just place as much as you can.)_

sections.title: Objective Card Setup and Resources
sections.text: Each player sets up using the Setup side of their objective card, then flips it to its Objective side. Each player may also rearrange their resource tokens. If player setups affect each other, resolve them in turn order. _(To speed up setup, feel free to do all this simultaneously!)_

sections.title: Objective Marker
sections.text: Each player places their objective marker on the Power track space as shown at the top of their objective card. In Act III, only players with a "C" Fate do this step.

sections.title: Chapter Track and Action Cards
sections.text: Place the Chapter track tile on its side that lists the current Act. Place the chapter marker on its "1" space. Draw and discard action cards exactly as in `rule:3.2.2.10`-`rule:3.2.2.11`.

sections.title: The Arc of Play
sections.text:
In a game of Arcs, you play through a number of **chapters**, usually three to five. Each chapter is made up of several **rounds**.

Broadly, in a round, each player will take one **turn** by playing an action card to do various actions, starting with the player who has initiative. After everyone takes a turn, players check who gets initiative for the next round. You'll learn more in **Playing a Chapter** (`rule-relative:Playing a Chapter`)!

Keep playing rounds until everyone runs out of action cards in their hand. At this point, the chapter ends, players gain Power from ambitions they fulfilled, and everyone draws a new hand of cards. You'll learn more in **Ending a Chapter** (`rule-relative:Ending a Chapter`)!

sections.title: Power & Ambitions
sections.text:
Players gain Power by fulfilling **ambitions**. The player with the initiative marker may choose to declare the ambition shown on the action card they play on their turn, marking the matching ambition box on the right map edge.

At the end of the chapter, players gain Power from declared ambitions that they fulfilled best. It doesn't matter whether another player declared an ambition—anyone can fulfill it.

sections.title: Clusters
sections.text: The map is made of 6 **clusters**. Each cluster has 4 **systems**: 3 **planets** and 1 **gate**, which lists the cluster number.

sections.title: Adjacency
sections.text: A system is **adjacent** to other systems sharing a thin border. Adjacency is most important when moving (`rule-relative:Standard Actions$Move`).

sections.title: Gates
sections.text: Each gate is adjacent to the 3 planets in its cluster and to the gates of its 2 neighboring clusters.

sections.title: Planets
sections.text: Each planet is adjacent to the gate in its cluster, and it is adjacent to one or both neighboring planets. Planets separated by a thick, irregular border are not adjacent.

sections.title: Planets
sections.text: Each **planet** has a **planet type**, along with 1 or 2 **building slots** where you can build cities and starports. _(Each planet also has an ***ID symbol*** of `symbol:arrow`, `symbol:hex`, or `symbol:moon`, used in expansions.)_

sections.title: Out of Play
sections.text: In setup, 1 or 2 clusters are covered with **out-of-play markers** on its planets and a **path marker** on its gate. These clusters are out of play in every way. The path marker joins together the gates of the two neighboring clusters, allowing for movement between them in a single move. The center of the map with the Arcs logo is not in play.

sections.title: Resources & Cities
sections.text:
There are 5 types of **resources** matching the 5 planet types. Usually, you gain them by taxing cities (**Tax**, `rule-relative:Standard Actions$Tax`) and raiding Rivals in battle (**Battle**, `rule-relative:Standard Actions$Battle`).

Resources can be spent for various actions (**Resources**, `rule-relative:Resources`), and some of them add to the **Tycoon**, **Keeper**, and **Empath** ambitions (`rule:6.2.1`).

You hold resource tokens in the **resource slots** on your player board. As you build **cities**, you open resource slots and uncover Power bonuses for winning ambitions.

sections.title: Agents & The Court
sections.text:
Your agents are the bureaucrats and diplomats that administer your cities and influence powerful interests in the Reach.

Through play, you can place agents on cards in the **Court**, a row of cards along the edge of the map (**Influence**, `rule-relative:Standard Actions$Influence`). If you have the most agents on a card in the Court, you can take it (**Secure**, `rule-relative:Standard Actions$Secure`).

sections.title: Fresh
sections.text: Pieces start off **fresh**—ships are fresh when standing upright, and buildings are fresh on their fully colored side.

sections.title: Damaged and Destroyed
sections.text: By battling, fresh pieces can become **damaged**, shown by flipping or tipping it over. If a damaged piece is damaged again, it is **destroyed**, removing it from the map.

sections.title: Control
sections.text: You **control** a system and its contents if you have ***more fresh ships*** there than each **Rival** _(other player)_. On a tie, no one controls the system.

sections.title: Benefits of Control
sections.text: Controlling a system lets you tax Rival cities there and capture their agents, restricts how their ships move, and damages pieces they build (`rule-relative:Standard Actions$Tax`-`rule-relative:Standard Actions$Move`).

sections.title: Trophies
sections.text: If you **destroy** a Rival's pieces, put them in the **Trophies box** on your player board. Trophies add to the **Warlord** ambition. Actions such as Battle (`rule-relative:Standard Actions$Battle`) let you destroy Rival pieces.

sections.title: Captives
sections.text: If you **capture** a Rival's agents, put them in the **Captives box** on your player board. Captives add to the **Tyrant** ambition. Actions such as Tax (`rule-relative:Standard Actions$Tax`) and Secure (`rule-relative:Standard Actions$Secure`) let you capture Rival agents.

sections.title: Playing a Chapter
sections.text: A game of Arcs lasts up to 5 **chapters**. In each chapter, you play some number of **rounds**. In a round, each player takes one **turn**, starting with the player with the initiative marker. Broadly, on your turn, you must play 1 **action card**, which lets you take one or more actions. At the end of the round, the initiative marker might go to a new player based on which cards were played. Keep playing rounds until everyone runs out of action cards. At this point, the chapter ends (`rule-relative:Ending a Chapter`).

sections.title: Step 1: Player with Initiative Takes Turn
Lead Card
trail: Step 1: Player with Initiative Takes Turn
sections.text:
As the player with initiative, you must play one action card face up as the **lead card**. You may take one action (`rule-relative:Standard Actions`) for each **action pip** on the lead card based on its suit:

  - **Administration** pips can **tax**, **repair**, or **influence**.
  - **Aggression** pips can **battle**, **move**, or **secure**.
  - **Construction** pips can **build** or **repair**.
  - **Mobilization** pips can **move** or **influence**.

Place the card in the “Lead” card slot on the left map edge, so players can reference it during the round.

sections.title: Passing Initiative
trail: Step 1: Player with Initiative Takes Turn
sections.text: If you have the initiative, but you have no cards in your hand or just choose to skip your turn, you must **pass the initiative**. When you pass the initiative, give the initiative marker to the next clockwise player who has any cards in their hand, then immediately end the round. The player who now has initiative will play the lead card of the new round.

sections.title: Early Chapter End
trail: Step 1: Player with Initiative Takes Turn
sections.text: If everyone with cards in their hand passes consecutively, discard all action cards and end the chapter (`rule-relative:Ending a Chapter`).

sections.title: Declaring an Ambition
trail: Step 1: Player with Initiative Takes Turn
sections.text: If you have the initiative, you may declare the ambition shown on your lead card before taking ***any*** actions. Then, place the zero marker onto the lead card to cover the **card number** in its top-left corner—its card number is now 0.

sections.title: Declaration
trail: Step 1: Player with Initiative Takes Turn
sections.text: To **declare an ambition**, take the highest-number ambition marker from the Available Markers section on the right map edge, and place it in the ambition box of the declared ambition.

sections.title: Ambitions by Card
trail: Step 1: Player with Initiative Takes Turn
sections.text:
Most action cards have an ambition, depending on their card number:
\- The “1” cards have ***no*** ambition. _(Four players only.)_
\- The “2” through 6” cards let you declare the ***matching*** ambition. _(They are listed in `rule:6.2.1`.)_
\- The “7” cards let you declare ***any*** ambition. _(Four players only.)_

sections.title: Ambitions are Limited
trail: Step 1: Player with Initiative Takes Turn
sections.text: You cannot declare an ambition if all ambitions markers are already placed.

sections.title: Turn Order
sections.text: After the player with initiative takes their turn, each other player in clockwise order takes a turn. Players with no cards in their hand skip their turn.

sections.title: Non-Lead Card
sections.text: On your turn, you must play an action card in one of three ways: Surpass, Copy, or Pivot. Place the card in the “Surpass, Copy, or Pivot” card slot on the left map edge, so players can reference it during the round.

sections.title: Surpass
sections.text: Play an action card face up of the lead card's suit. Its card number must be higher than the lead card. You may take actions up to the number of action pips on ***your card***.

sections.title: Copy
sections.text: Play any action card face down. You may take only one action of ***the lead card***.

sections.title: Pivot
sections.text: Play an action card face up that is not of the lead card's suit. It can have any card number. You may take only one action on ***your card***.

sections.title: Seizing the Initiative
sections.text:
When you play a card, before taking **any** actions, you can **seize the initiative** from the player who holds it by doing one of the following:

  - **You may choose to play an extra action card.** Place it face down beside the card
    you played as a reminder. You do not get actions for it.
  - **You Surpass with a “7” action card.** You still get to take its actions. _(Only
    four-player games have “7” cards.)_

sections.title: Seize the Initiative
sections.text: To **seize the initiative**, take the initiative marker and lay it down to show it is seized. For the rest of this round, players cannot seize the initiative.

sections.title: No Self Seize
sections.text: The player with initiative cannot seize the initiative.

sections.title: Step 3: Check Initiative
sections.text: After everyone has taken a turn, check whether the initiative marker goes to a new player.

sections.title: Surpassed
sections.text: If no one seized the initiative this round, give the initiative to the player who ***Surpassed with the highest card number.*** If no one Surpassed, the initiative stays with its holder.

sections.title: Seized
sections.text: If someone seized the initiative this round, that player keeps the initiative.

sections.title: Step 4: Discard Cards & Check for New Round
Discard Cards
trail: Step 4: Discard Cards & Check for New Round
sections.text: Discard all played action cards, and any action card used to seize the initiative, into the action discard pile on the map ***face down***.

sections.title: End of Round
trail: Step 4: Discard Cards & Check for New Round
sections.text: If any players have any action cards left in their hand, start the next round. Otherwise, end the chapter (`rule-relative:Ending a Chapter`).

sections.title: End Condition
sections.text: The chapter ends when everyone runs out of action cards or when everyone with cards passes the initiative.

sections.title: End Procedure
sections.text: When the chapter ends, resolve the following steps:

sections.title: Step 1: Score Ambitions
sections.text:
Score each ambition that has any number of ambition markers in its ambition box on the map:

  - **Tycoon.** Have the most total Fuel and Material icons from resources and Guild
    cards.
  - **Tyrant.** Have the most Captives on your player board _(gained from_ **taxing**
    _and_ **securing**_)._
  - **Warlord.** Have the most Trophies on your player board _(gained in_
    **battle**_)._
  - **Keeper.** Have the most Relic icons from resources and Guild cards.
  - **Empath.** Have the most Psionic icons from resources and Guild cards.

The player who gets ***first place*** for the ambition gains the higher Power shown on all its ambition markers. The player who gets ***second place*** for it gains the lower Power shown on all its ambition markers. Show the Power you gained by advancing your Power marker on the Power track on the bottom edge of the map.

sections.title: Ties
sections.text: On a tie for first place, all tied players get second place. _(Other players do not place and gain no Power.)_  On a tie for second place, the tied players do not place and gain no Power.

sections.title: Qualifying
sections.text: You cannot gain Power from an ambition if you have none of the thing it is counting. _(For example, if Warlord is declared and nobody has Trophies, nobody gains Power.)_

sections.title: Bonus City Power
sections.text: Each time you get first place in an ambition _(not tied)_, gain 2 extra Power if the “+2 to won ambitions” city slot on your player board is uncovered, or gain 5 extra if both the “+2 to won ambitions” and “+3 to won ambitions” city slots on your player board are uncovered.

sections.title: Two-Player Scoring
sections.text: During setup with 2 players, 6 resources matching the planets with out-of-play markers are placed on the ambition boxes. For scoring, count these resources as if a third player had them. Weapons on the Warlord box count as Trophies. Otherwise, these resources are out of play.

sections.title: Step 2: Clean Up & Flip Ambition
sections.text: Resolve the following steps:

sections.title: Step 1: Warlord and Tyrant
sections.text: If Warlord was scored, return all Trophies. If Tyrant was scored, return all Captives.

sections.title: Step 2: Return Ambitions
sections.text: Return all ambition markers to the Available Markers spaces on the map.

sections.title: Step 3: Flip Ambition
sections.text: Flip over the ambition marker with the ***lowest Power*** that hasn't been flipped yet to its side with more Power.

sections.title: Step 3: End Game or Advance Chapter
sections.text: The game ends if any player has at least ***27 Power*** (4 players), ***30 Power*** (3 players), or ***33 Power*** (2 players), or if the chapter marker is currently on Chapter 5.

sections.title: Determining a Winner
trail: Step 3: End Game or Advance Chapter
sections.text: If the game ends, the player with the most Power is the winner. On a tie, the tied player earliest in turn order is the winner.

sections.title: Next Chapter
trail: Step 3: End Game or Advance Chapter
sections.text: If the game does not end, advance the chapter marker to the next space.

sections.title: Step 4: Draw Cards
sections.text: Shuffle all of the action cards. Each player draws a hand of ***6 action cards***. Discard all action cards not in players' hands into the action discard pile on the map ***face down***, then shuffle it. The player with initiative starts the next chapter.

sections.title: Two-Player Mulligans
sections.text: In games with 2 players, after drawing, the player ***without*** initiative may discard their hand of 6 action cards to draw a new hand of 6 action cards. They must accept this new hand.

sections.title: Tax
sections.text: The Tax action appears on Administration cards.

sections.title: Tax
sections.text: To take this action, resolve the following steps:

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Choose a Loyal city or choose a Rival city you control.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Gain 1 resource of the city's planet type from the supply.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: If you tax a Rival city, you also capture 1 agent of that Rival from their supply, even if you didn't gain the resource.

sections.title: Captives
sections.text: Place captured agents in the Captives box on your player board. They add to your **Tyrant** ambition (`rule-relative:Ending a Chapter`).

sections.title: Tax Limit
sections.text: You cannot tax a city more than once per turn.

sections.title: Build
sections.text: The Build action appears on Construction cards.

sections.title: Build
sections.text:
You may build a **building** or a **ship**:

  - **Building:** Place 1 starport or city in an empty building slot in a system with a
    Loyal piece. When building a city, use the leftmost city on your player board.
  - **Ship:** Place 1 ship at a Loyal starport. Each starport can only build one ship
    per turn.

sections.title: Control
sections.text: When you build anything in a system that is controlled by anyone other than you, place the piece damaged.

sections.title: Move
sections.text: The Move action appears on Mobilization and Aggression cards.

sections.title: Move
sections.text: Move any number of Loyal ships from one system to an adjacent system.

sections.title: Catapult Move
sections.text: If you move from a system with a Loyal starport, you may take **Catapult moves**—keep moving the ships as much as you want, dropping them off as you want, until they move to a gate controlled by anyone else or they move to any planet.

sections.title: Out-of-Play Clusters
sections.text: You cannot move into any systems in out-of-play clusters. The path marker placed on out-of-play gates makes its two neighboring gates adjacent.

sections.title: Repair
sections.text: The Repair action appears on Construction and Administration cards.

sections.title: Repair
sections.text: Stand up 1 damaged Loyal ship, or flip over 1 damaged Loyal building. _(This can be anywhere on the map!)_

sections.title: Influence
sections.text: The Influence action appears on Mobilization and Administration cards.

sections.title: Influence
sections.text: Place 1 agent on any card in the Court. _(The Court is the card row along the map edge.)_

sections.title: Secure
sections.text: The Secure action appears on Aggression cards.

sections.title: Secure
sections.text: To take this action, resolve the following steps:

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Take 1 card from the Court if you have more Loyal agents on it than each Rival. Return all Loyal agents on it to your supply, and capture all Rival agents from the secured card.

sections.title: Captives
sections.text: Put agents you capture in the Captives box on your player board. They add to your **Tyrant** ambition (`rule-relative:Ending a Chapter`).

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Resolve its **When Secured** action, if any. If it says to discard it, place it in a face-up Court discard pile near the Court deck.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Draw a card from the Court deck and place it face up in the Court in the same spot as the secured card.

sections.title: Battle
sections.text: The Battle action appears on Aggression cards.

sections.title: Battle
sections.text: To take this action, resolve the following steps:

sections.title: Step 1: Choose Battle System
sections.text: Choose 1 system that has any Loyal ships. This is the battle system. These are your **attacking ships**.

sections.title: Step 2: Choose Defender
sections.text: Choose 1 Rival whose pieces are in the battle system. These are their **defending pieces**.

sections.title: Step 3: Collect Dice
sections.text:
For each attacking ship, you may collect 1 assault, skirmish, or raid die.
\- **Assault dice** damage the defender quickly at some cost to you.
\- **Skirmish dice** damage the defender slowly but keep you safe.
\- **Raid dice** steal stuff from the defender and might damage them but are risky.

sections.title: Raid Dice Limit
sections.text: You can only collect raid dice if there are ***defending buildings*** or if the defender has no Loyal buildings in any systems on the map.

sections.title: Step 4: Roll and Resolve Dice
sections.text: Roll the collected dice. You must resolve all rolled faces in this order:

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Hit any of your ***attacking ships*** once per `symbol:selfhit`.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: If you rolled any number of `symbol:intercept`, the defender **intercepts** you—hit any of your ***attacking ships*** once per fresh defending ship. _(This can only happen once per battle!)_

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Hit any of their ***defending ships*** once per `symbol:hit`. Once no defending ships remain, hit any of their defending buildings instead.

sections.title: Step 4
sections.text: Hit any of their ***defending buildings*** once per `symbol:buildinghit`.

sections.title: Step 5
sections.text: Raid their ***resources and cards*** by spending `symbol:key`, if you have any attacking ships left (**Raiding**, `rule-relative:Standard Actions$Battle$Raiding.`).

sections.title: Damaging Pieces
sections.text: If you hit a fresh piece, it becomes **damaged**—tip it over if it's a ship or flip it over if it's a building.

sections.title: Destroying Pieces
sections.text: If you hit a damaged piece, it is **destroyed**—remove it. The attacker takes destroyed defending pieces as Trophies. The defender takes destroyed attacking pieces as Trophies.

sections.title: Trophies
sections.text: Place pieces taken as Trophies in the Trophies box on the respective player board. These add to the **Warlord** ambition (`rule-relative:Ending a Chapter`).

sections.title: Destroying Cities
sections.text: If you destroy a city—even outside battle—do the following:

sections.title: Step 1: Provoke Outrage
sections.text: Discard all resources and Guild cards you have of that city's planet type, placing the discarded cards in a face-up Court discard pile near the Court deck. Place an agent to cover the Outrage icon of that city's planet type on your player board—that resource is now **Outraged**.

sections.title: Outrage
sections.text: You cannot spend Outraged resources for their normal Prelude action (`rule-relative:Standard Actions$Battle$Destroying Cities.`).

sections.title: Step 2: Ransack the Court
sections.text: Secure any card that has ***any number*** of the defender's agents. Take all Rival agents on the card as ***Trophies***, not Captives.

sections.title: Raiding
sections.text: If any attacking ships remain after taking hits, you may spend `symbol:key` you rolled to steal resources and Guild cards from the defender, one at a time, by spending the number `symbol:key` of in its **raid cost**, shown above the resource slot on the player board or in the top-left corner of the Guild card (`rule-relative:Guild Cards$Card Anatomy$Raid Cost.`).

sections.title: Prelude Actions
sections.text: Many cards and all resources (`rule-relative:Resources`) give **Prelude actions**. On cards, these actions begin with **“Prelude:”**

sections.title: Timing
sections.text: Your Prelude begins once you play an action card and ends once you spend an action pip from your played card.

sections.title: Limits
sections.text:
You can take any number of Prelude actions, with two limits:
  - Resources spent in Prelude return to the supply at the ***end*** of your Prelude,
    so you cannot regain them until then.
  - You cannot use Prelude actions on cards that you secured from the Court in the same
    Prelude.

sections.title: Discarding Cards
sections.text: Some Prelude actions on cards make you discard the card. Place it in a face-up Court discard pile near the Court deck.

sections.title: New Actions
sections.text: Cards can give you a **new action** followed by the name of a standard action in parentheses, such as **Assassinate (Battle)**. When you would take the standard action by spending an action pip or resource, you may instead take the new action.

sections.title: Modifiers
sections.text: Cards can give you **modifiers** to standard actions, which are shown in **bold**, such as “In **battle**, collect 1 extra die.”

sections.title: New Actions
sections.text: Modifiers do not modify new actions, but they do modify standard actions that are within new actions.

sections.title: Play Steps
sections.text: Modifiers can also affect critical play steps, such as **setup** (`rule:3.1`), **scoring** (`rule:6.2.1`), **declare an ambition** (`rule:5.1`), and **seize the initiative** (`rule:5.2.3`).

sections.title: Prelude Actions
sections.text:
In your turn's Prelude (`rule-relative:Other Actions$Prelude Actions`), you may spend any number and mix of your resource tokens to optionally use their actions:
  - **Material:** Take a Build or Repair action.
  - **Fuel:** Take a Move action.
  - **Weapon:** This turn, you may spend any action pips from your card play to take Battle
    actions.
  - **Relic:** Take a Secure action.
  - **Psionic:** Take an action listed on the lead card.

sections.title: Slots
sections.text: Resources are held in resource slots.

sections.title: Placing Resources
sections.text: When you take a resource, place it in an empty resource slot of yours. At this time, you may rearrange any resources in your resource slots, but you must discard resources you cannot hold.

sections.title: Returning Cities
sections.text: If a city returns to your player board and covers a resource slot, rearrange and discard resources as described in `rule-relative:Resources$Slots$Placing Resources.`.

sections.title: Raid Cost
sections.text: Each resource slot has a **raid cost**: the number of `symbol:key` attacker in battle must spend to steal the resource.

sections.title: Access
sections.text: Some cards say they hold resources. These resources can be spent and add to ambitions,  but they cannot be stolen in battle unless explicitly allowed. If a card holding resources  is stolen, the resources on the card stay on it. If it is buried, discarded, or scrapped,  the resources on it return to the supply.

sections.title: Removal
sections.text: If a card holding resources is stolen, the resources on the card stay on it. If it is buried, discarded or scrapped, the resources on it return to the supply.

sections.title: Acquisition
sections.text: You can gain Guild cards by influencing them in the Court and then securing them (`rule-relative:Standard Actions$Secure`).

sections.title: Card Anatomy
sections.text: Guild cards have 3 parts: their **suit**, **rules**, and **raid cost**.

sections.title: Suit
sections.text: This suit icon matches 1 of the 5 resources. It adds to ambitions just like resources—Material and Fuel cards add to the Tycoon ambition, Relic cards add to the Keeper ambition, and Psionic cards add to the Empath ambition. Weapon cards do not add to any ambitions.

sections.title: Rules
sections.text: Guild cards give new actions and modifiers (`rule-relative:Other Actions$New Actions`-`rule-relative:Other Actions$Modifiers`).

sections.title: Raid Cost
sections.text: This shows how many `symbol:key` an attacker must spend in battle in order to steal the card.

sections.title: Leaders & Lore
sections.text:
After playing a game or two, you're ready to play with **Leaders and Lore**! This mode gives players wild, unique abilities, but they can be hard to handle if you're starting out. ***Really, don't play your first game with Leaders and Lore.***

  - Your **leader card** gives you unique powers, starting pieces, and starting resources.
  - **Lore cards** give persistent powers. They don't have a guild icon or raid cost, so they
    do not add to ambitions and cannot be stolen.

sections.title: Setup
sections.text: Replace the Starting Placement (`rule:3.1.2.3`) and Starting Resources (`rule:3.1.2.4`) steps of the base game setup with the following:

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Lay out **lore cards** and **leader cards** in face-up rows, each with cards equal to the ***players plus one***.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: In reverse turn order—start with the player to the right of the player with initiative, and go counterclockwise—each player may take 1 leader or lore card.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Continue this until each player has 1 leader card and 1 lore card. You cannot take a leader card if you already have one, and you cannot take a lore card if you already have one.

sections.title: Extra Lore
sections.text: If you want to increase chaos and uniqueness even more, you can let players choose a second lore card. Just add 1 extra lore card per player to the starting row, and keep choosing cards until each player has 1 leader card and 2 lore cards.

sections.title: Step 4
sections.text: Each player places their starting pieces onto the map in the systems marked on the setup card as shown in the ***A, B, and C boxes shown on their leader card.*** _Pips under a ship icon show how many ships to place._

sections.title: Step 5
sections.text: Each player gains the ***2 resource tokens shown on their leader card***, placing them in their 2 leftmost resource slots in the order shown.

sections.title: Step 6
sections.text: If any leaders have extra setup steps, players perform them in turn order.

sections.title: The Blighted Reach
sections.text:
The galaxy is in crisis. The **Empire** is crumbling. The **Blight** is spreading through the Reach, destroying everything it touches. What is it? What does it want?

Some believe this is the end. Others, just the beginning. In this time of chaos, new movements bloom loud like desert flowers, promising safety, liberation, communion, or simply the honor of glorious death in the struggle. What will you promise? What is your **Fate**?

***We strongly recommend*** you play at least one game of single-session _Arcs_ before the campaign. All players should be comfy with the base game. Otherwise, expect a long, tedious first game.

sections.title: Acts
sections.text: A campaign of Arcs lasts for three games, called **Acts**. Campaign Acts end differently from single-session games.

sections.title: Fixed Length
sections.text: Don't end an Act after 5 chapters. Instead, Acts I and II end after ***3 chapters***, and Act III ends after ***4 chapters***. Don't end an Act early if a player gains enough Power. Ignore the thresholds on the Power track.

sections.title: Fates
sections.text: While setting up Act I, you choose an “A” Fate. You might play this Fate for all three Acts or switch to a new one. If you switch Fate after Act I, you'll choose a **“B” Fate**, and if you switch Fate after Act II, you'll choose a **“C” Fate**.

sections.title: Determining a Winner
sections.text: At the end of Act III, the winner is the player with the most Power ***accumulated over all three Acts***. You can also win by completing a final objective (`rule-relative:The Campaign$Final Objective`).

sections.title: Tiebreakers
sections.text: Break a Power tie in favor of “A” Fates over “B” Fates, and “B” Fates over “C” Fates. Break a further tie in turn order.

sections.title: Objective
sections.text: In Acts I and II, your Fate gives you an **objective**. During setup, place your **objective marker** on the **starting space** on the Power track shown at the top of your objective card. Sometimes, the starting space changes based on the number of players, shown by the `symbol:player` symbols.

sections.title: Completion
sections.text: Your objective card gives you ways to **advance** your objective marker, moving it down the Power track toward 0 Power. When it reaches 0 Power, you complete your objective.

sections.title: Winning Ambitions
sections.text: Some objectives want you to **win** an ambition—this means you get first place, so you're ***not tied***.

sections.title: Intermission
sections.text: After Acts I and II, there is an **Intermission**. In it, you gain a bonus for completing your objective, you might choose a new Fate, and most damaged pieces are destroyed. If you failed your objective, you lose Power equal to the space of your objective marker on the Power track.

sections.title: Grand Ambitions
sections.text: In Act III, “A” or “B” Fates give two **grand ambitions**, shown by gold crosshairs. These give you more ways to gain Power and do not use the objective marker.

sections.title: Timing
sections.text: At the end of a chapter, grand ambitions are scored at the same time as declared ambitions.

sections.title: Amount
sections.text: If you fulfilled one grand ambition, gain the lower amount of Power shown under the current chapter on the Chapter track. If you fulfilled both, gain the higher amount.

sections.title: Personal
sections.text: Your grand ambitions are always active—you do not need to declare them. Rivals cannot gain Power from them.

sections.title: Final Objective
sections.text: In Act III, “C” Fates have a **final objective**.

sections.title: Outright Victory
sections.text: At the end of a chapter, after scoring ambitions, ***you win the game*** if your final objective is complete by having your objective marker at “0” ***and you have at least 1 Power.***

sections.title: Tiebreakers
sections.text: Winning by completing a final objective supersedes winning by having the most Power. If multiple players would win the game by completing their final objective, the winner is the player among them with the most Power.

sections.title: Power Victory
sections.text: If you have a final objective, you can still win at the end of Chapter 4 by simply having the most Power.

sections.title: Rules Booklet
sections.text: As you play, your Fate will add many cards to the **rules booklet**. The booklet is double-sided. You can use one side for Edict cards and the other side for Law and Summit cards. In rare cases where you run out of space on one side for a specific card type, you can use the other side. As you add cards to this booklet, make sure to explain them aloud, since these rules affect everyone.

sections.title: Protected Guild Cards
sections.text: Some Guild cards in the campaign are **protected**, shown by an “X” icon in place of their raid cost.

sections.title: Cannot Remove
sections.text: Protected Guild cards cannot be removed from the holder's play area ***unless the holder Provokes Outrage*** of its suit or if the Guild card is referenced explicitly by name.

sections.title: One Each
sections.text: If you are prompted to **attach** a card, place above a card in the Court that does not have an attached card.

sections.title: Securing
sections.text: When you **secure** a card, also secure its attached card. If both have When Secured actions, resolve them in either order.

sections.title: Forced Attach
sections.text: If you are forced to attach a card but you cannot fulfill all of the requirements to attach it, you still attach it, ignoring the fewest requirements to attach it.

sections.title: Removal from Court
sections.text: If a card is removed from the Court in any way and it has an attached card, refill the Court by sliding down the attached card. Place all agents from the removed card onto the previously attached card. If an ***attached card*** is removed, nothing happens to the card it was attached to.

sections.title: Frozen
sections.text: Some resources are frozen. The player holding the frozen resources cannot remove them from the freezing piece except with scrap or in ways stated by the freezing piece or other pieces that reference it. _(For example, Govern the Imperial Reach can let the First Regent give Weapons from the Imperial Trust.)_

sections.title: Counting
sections.text: When you are prompted to count how many resources you have, count ***everything in your play area***, including on cards and on tiles such as the First Regent tile.

sections.title: Harm
sections.text: Some rules refer to **harm**—this means choosing as defender in battle, damaging, destroying, or hitting, except against yourself.

sections.title: Tokens
sections.text: Many Fates add new punchboard **tokens**.

sections.title: Cannot Harm
sections.text: These tokens cannot be **harmed** unless they say otherwise.

sections.title: Not Loyal
sections.text: By default, tokens added by Fates are not **Loyal**. However, some do say they are Loyal—you treat them as being your player color, and Rivals treat them as Rival pieces. You can **build** buildings at Loyal tokens, you can **repair** damaged Loyal tokens, and they fulfill the need for Loyal pieces found in rules such as the Empire's Presence Law (`rule-relative:The Empire$Control & Command$Presence Law.`).

sections.title: The Empire
sections.text:
Everyone starts as a **Regent** of a crumbling galactic **Empire**, shown by their Regent title card tucked into their Fate card.

One Regent is the **First Regent**, who governs the Empire (`rule-relative:The Empire`) and holds the **Imperial Trust** (`rule-relative:Edicts$Collect Imperial Demand$Resources.`), resources they collect from Regents as tribute for the distant Emperor.

A Regent can become an **Outlaw** by calling a Summit (`rule-relative:Summits`). Outlaws can be attacked by the Empire, but they can battle Regents freely and don't pay into the Imperial Trust.

sections.title: Imperial Sovereignty
sections.text: The Empire controls all systems that have ***any number of fresh Imperial ships***, ignoring all players' Loyal ships.

sections.title: Presence Law
sections.text: On a Regent's turn, they **Command the Imperial Fleet** following the **Presence Law:** In systems ***with Loyal pieces***, they control the system if it is Empire-controlled and can take actions with Imperial ships there—**move** and **repair** them, **battle** with them, **build** at them, and **tax** cities they control.

sections.title: Ignoring the Presence Law
sections.text: If a rule lets you ignore the Presence Law, you Command the Imperial Fleet in all systems, even those with no Loyal pieces.

sections.title: First Regent's Privilege
sections.text: The First Regent controls all Empire-controlled systems for the purpose of ambitions, objectives, and events (`rule-relative:Events & the Imperial Council`).

sections.title: Movement Law
sections.text: Regents follow the **Movement Law:** Regents can only **move** 1 Imperial ship for each Loyal ship they are moving along with them at the same time to the same system.

sections.title: Empire Control
sections.text: Empire control of gates ends the Catapult moves of Outlaw pieces, but not Regent or Imperial pieces.

sections.title: Regent Control
sections.text: Regent control of gates ends the Catapult moves of Outlaw pieces and Rival Regent pieces alone, but not Imperial pieces or mixed Regent and Imperial pieces.

sections.title: Outlaw Control
sections.text: Outlaw control of gates ends the Catapult moves of Regent and Imperial pieces alike.

sections.title: Truce Law
sections.text: Regents follow the **Truce Law:** Regents cannot **harm** Imperial ships except for hits they take as attacking ships in battle, and they cannot **harm** or **tax** Rival Regents in systems with Imperial ships.

sections.title: Empire May Attack
sections.text: When a Regent ***attacks*** in battle, they ***may*** add Imperial ships in the battle system to their attacking ships.

sections.title: Empire Must Defend
sections.text: When a Regent ***defends*** in battle, they ***must*** add Imperial ships in the battle system to their defending ships.

sections.title: Battling the Empire
sections.text: Outlaws may choose either a Regent or the Empire as defender. If the Empire is defending, the defending pieces are the Imperial ships in the battle system.

sections.title: Trophies
sections.text: If the Empire is defending, the First Regent takes any destroyed pieces of the Outlaw as Trophies. If there is no First Regent, they return to the Outlaw.

sections.title: The Blight
sections.text: The Blight is a mysterious entity spreading through the Reach. No one knows what it wants or how to communicate with it. In Crises (`rule-relative:Crises`), the Blight hits ships. In the Intermission (`rule-relative:Intermission`), it destroys buildings in systems with no ships.

sections.title: Harming & Trophies
sections.text: Blight can be **harmed**—battled, hit, damaged, and destroyed. However, it is ***Tough***—it takes 2 hits to damage or destroy. One hit does nothing. Take Blight that you destroy as Trophies.

sections.title: Battling
sections.text: If you choose the Blight as defender in battle, all Blight in the battle system are defending pieces. Blight is hit with `symbol:hit` but not `symbol:buildinghit`. Blight does not intercept.

sections.title: Catapult Movement
sections.text: Players taking a Catapult **move** must end it if they move into a gate with fresh or damaged Blight, like if a Rival controlled the gate.

sections.title: Empty Supply
sections.text: If you must place Blight but the supply is empty, take it from the player who has the most Blight Trophies.

sections.title: The Free States
sections.text: As the Empire crumbles, some people have escaped its grip, declared independence, and formed the **Free States**.

sections.title: Actions
sections.text: You may take actions with Free buildings ***that you control***—**tax** Free cities, **build** ships at Free starports and Catapult **move** from them, and **repair** Free cities and starports.

sections.title: Harming & Trophies
sections.text: Just like players' buildings, Free buildings can be **harmed**—battled, hit, damaged, and destroyed. Take Free buildings you destroy as Trophies.

sections.title: Battling
sections.text: If you choose the Free States as defender in battle, all Free buildings in the battle system are defending pieces. They take hits from rolled dice like players' buildings.

sections.title: Raiding
sections.text: You may raid the Free States. You may gain exactly 1 resource matching its planet type by spending `symbol:key`. This counts as stealing. You cannot gain multiple resources from the Free States in the same battle.

sections.title: Empty Supply
sections.text: In the rare event that you must place a Free building but the supply is empty, use a proxy piece.

sections.title: Events & the Imperial Council
sections.text:
There are three kinds of events: Summits, Crises, and Edicts.

  - During a **Summit**, players can make deals to exchange pieces and favors in a freeform
    manner.
  - During the **Crises**, the Blight attacks ships on the map, and some Guild and Vox cards
    cause chaos.
  - During the **Edicts**, the First Regent governs the Empire. Over time, more Edicts are
    added.

Events can be triggered by playing an **Event card** or securing the **Imperial Council card** from the Court (`rule-relative:Events & the Imperial Council$Imperial Council`).

sections.title: Event Cards
sections.text: Event cards are a new kind of action card added during setup.

sections.title: Playing an Event Card
sections.text: On your turn, you may play an Event card. ***You cannot Lead it, Copy with it, or discard it to seize the initiative.***

sections.title: Actions from an Event Card
sections.text: When you play an Event card, you may take actions exactly like you played the lead card.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.text: Your Event card gives you no actions if ***another Event card*** was played earlier this round or if the ***Imperial Council*** was secured earlier this round and is currently tucked (`rule-relative:Events & the Imperial Council$Imperial Council`).

sections.title: Cannot Scrap
sections.text: Event cards cannot be scrapped.

sections.title: Two-Player Mulligans
sections.text: When you take a mulligan in a two-player game, you must keep any Event cards in your hand and only draw the number of action cards you discarded.

sections.title: Resolution
sections.text: At the end of a round where any Event cards were played, do the following just after checking whether initiative changes:

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: The player with initiative may call the Summit (`rule-relative:Summits`).

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text:
The player with initiative rolls the event and number dice and resolves the event die as follows:
\- If `symbol:crisis` is rolled, resolve **Crises** (`rule-relative:Crises`).
\- If `symbol:edict` is rolled, resolve **Edicts** (`rule-relative:Edicts`).

sections.title: Imperial Council Overrides Events
sections.text: If the Imperial Council (`rule-relative:Events & the Imperial Council$Imperial Council`) is secured during the same round as any Event cards are played, resolve the Council and do not resolve the Event card.

sections.title: Imperial Council
sections.text:
The **Imperial Council** is a card in the Court with two sides: In Session and Decided. In each Act, it starts **In Session**. Securing the Imperial Council flips it to its **Decided** side.
It flips back to In Session at the start of an Act (`rule:3.2`), and you can flip it to In Session if you call a Summit and Petition the Council (`rule-relative:Summits$Call to Order$Petition the Council.`).
If it flips while tucked under a card, return it to the Court.

sections.title: In Session
sections.text: While the Imperial Council is In Session, players may influence and secure it.

sections.title: Decided
sections.text: While the Imperial Council is Decided, players cannot influence or secure it.

sections.title: Securing the Council
sections.text: When you **secure** the Council, flip it to **Decided** and tuck it under your played card as a reminder to resolve it later. At the end of that round, return the Imperial Council card to the Court on its Decided side, then resolve the following:

sections.title: Step 1: Summit
sections.text: You may call a Summit (`rule-relative:Summits`).

sections.title: Step 2: Become First Regent
sections.text: If you're a **Regent**, take the First Regent tile, keeping all resources on the Imperial Trust (`rule-relative:Edicts$Collect Imperial Demand$Resources.`).

sections.title: Step 3: Steal from Empire
sections.text: If you're an **Outlaw**, steal resources from the Imperial Trust on the First Regent tile, up to your number of empty resource slots. The First Regent loses 1 Power for each resource stolen.

sections.title: Step 4: Crises or Edicts
sections.text: You must choose to resolve either the **Crises** (`rule-relative:Crises`) or the **Edicts** (`rule-relative:Edicts`).

sections.title: Event Cards
sections.text: If the Imperial Council is secured in the same round as Event cards (`rule-relative:Events & the Imperial Council$Event Cards`) are played, resolve the Council and ignore the Event cards.

sections.title: Intrigue
sections.text: If the Imperial Council flips while tucked under a card, return it to the Court. _(You no longer resolve it at the end of this round!)_

sections.title: Immunity
sections.text: The Imperial Council cannot be buried, scrapped, or discarded.

sections.title: Summits
sections.text:
Event cards and the Imperial Council let players call the Summit. It has two parts: **Call to Order**, then **Negotiations**.

Broadly, in the Call to Order you can return **Favors**—Rival agents you have collected on your Fate card—to your Rivals to force them to take Negotiation actions, and you can interact with Imperial politics.

Then, in Negotiations, everyone can take Negotiation actions in a freeform manner, including giving each other Favors that can be returned in later Summits.

sections.title: Call to Order
sections.text: ***The player who called the Summit*** may take any number of Call to Order actions, listed below:

sections.title: Return Favors
sections.text: Return a Rival's Favors to their supply to force them to take Negotiation actions (`rule-relative:Summits$Negotiations$Negotiation Actions.`) you choose, ***targeting you***, in the way you choose. By default, each Negotiation action you force costs 1 Favor.

sections.title: Petition the Council
sections.text: Flip the Imperial Council card to its In Session side.

sections.title: Leave the Empire
sections.text: Flip your Regent title card to Outlaw. If you are the First Regent, give the First Regent tile to the Regent with the most Power. Resources stay in the Imperial Trust. ***If there are no Regents***, return all resources from the Imperial Trust to the supply, lose 1 Power per resource returned, and place the First Regent tile in the supply.

sections.title: Revive the Empire
sections.text: If there are no Regents, flip your Outlaw title card to Regent and take the First Regent tile.

sections.title: Negotiations
sections.text: After the Call to Order, ***all players*** may take any number of Negotiation actions listed below in a freeform manner. Each Negotiation action affects a Rival. To take a Negotiation action, you need the consent of the affected Rival.

sections.title: Cede Control
sections.text: Replace 1 Loyal piece on the map with 1 Rival piece of that type. You can only replace a Loyal building if no Loyal ships are in its system, and you cannot replace your last city, starport, or ship on the map.

sections.title: Delegate Authority
sections.text: Replace 1 Loyal agent on a card in the Court with a Rival's agent.

sections.title: Promise Favor
sections.text: Give 1 Loyal agent from your supply to a Rival, placing it on their Fate card. Rival agents on a Fate card are called **Favors**.

sections.title: Transfer Asset
sections.text: Give 1 Captive, Trophy, Favor, or resource you have to a Rival. If it is their Loyal piece, return it to their supply. Forcing you to give a resource with Return Favors (`rule-relative:Summits$Call to Order$Return Favors.`) costs Favors equal to its raid cost.

sections.title: Invite to Empire
sections.text: ***If you're the First Regent***, flip an Outlaw's title card to Regent.

sections.title: Multipart Negotiations
sections.text: You may agree with any players to simultaneously take any number of Negotiation actions that can be resolved immediately.

sections.title: Ending Negotiations
sections.text: If no one is negotiating, the player who called the Summit may call for them to start negotiating, wait briefly, and then count down from five seconds. If no one starts negotiating, the Summit ends.

sections.title: Crises
sections.text: Event cards and the Imperial Council can trigger the Crises. When the Crises are triggered, resolve the **Blight Crises**, then **Fate Crises**, and finally **Court Crises**.

sections.title: Blight Crises
sections.text: Each system with Blight has a **Blight Crisis**—each fresh Blight there deals 3 hits, and each damaged Blight there deals 1 hit.

sections.title: Hit Priority
sections.text: The Blight deals hits to Imperial ships first. If no Imperial ships remain, it deals each remaining hit to the Loyal ships of ***every player in its system.*** In both cases, fresh ships take hits before damaged ships.

sections.title: Fate Crises
sections.text: Some Fates add cards with **Crisis** text that are held by players. Resolve all of these cards in turn order.

sections.title: Court Crises
sections.text: The ***player with initiative*** rolls the event and number dice unless they were just rolled to  resolve an Event card. Resolve the **Crisis** text on each Vox card in the Court from left to right.

sections.title: Attached Cards
sections.text: If a Vox card has another Vox card attached to it (`rule-relative:Campaign Rules & Terms$Attaching Cards`), resolve the attached card first.

sections.title: Event & Number Dice
sections.text: Some Crises determine how they resolve using the icon and number on the event and number dice. Here are the key phrases that refer to these dice:

sections.title: Rolled Cluster
sections.text: The cluster rolled on the number die.

sections.title: Planets of the Rolled Symbol
sections.text: Each planet with the planet ID symbol (`symbol:arrow`/`symbol:hex`/`symbol:moon`) rolled on the event die.

sections.title: Rolled Planet
sections.text: The planet in the cluster rolled on the number die and the ID (`symbol:arrow`/`symbol:hex`/`symbol:moon`) rolled on the event die.

sections.title: If `symbol:arrow`/`symbol:hex`/`symbol:moon` Was Rolled
sections.text: Check whether this symbol was rolled on the event die.

sections.title: Removing Cards
sections.text: If a Crisis removes a card from the Court, return all agents on it and draw a card from the Court deck to refill the Court.

sections.title: Edicts
sections.text:
Event cards and the Imperial Council can trigger the Edicts. Resolve all Edicts in order from lowest number to highest.

The game starts with **Govern the Imperial Reach (Edict 03)** and **Guild Envoys Depart (Edict 00)** in two-player games.

sections.title: Govern the Imperial Reach
sections.text:
The First Regent must either enforce or change the Imperial **Policy** shown on this edict card.
- If they **enforce** it, they collect the listed **Imperial Demand** and then take the
  listed **Imperial Action**, as described through the rest of this section.

- If they **change** it, they choose a new Govern the Imperial Reach edict card to place on
  top of the other two cards.

sections.title: Collect Imperial Demand
sections.text:
The First Regent must take 1 piece from ***each Regent*** as shown by the Demand of the Imperial Policy, as follows:

  - **Peace:** Relics or Psionics
  - **Escalation:** Material, Fuel, or Weapons
  - **War:** Trophies or Captives, but ***not Regent*** or Imperial pieces

sections.title: Resources
sections.text: Resources go on the First Regent tile, adding to the Imperial Trust. The First Regent ***must also*** add 1 resource shown by the Demand to the Trust, if they have it. _(These resources have no raid cost, so they cannot be stolen in battle. However, cards such as Silver-Tongues can steal them, and Outlaws can steal them by securing the Imperial Council – see `rule-relative:Events & the Imperial Council$Imperial Council`. These resources return to the supply during the Intermission – see `rule-relative:Intermission$C. Clear Pieces$Step 2.`.)_

sections.title: Frozen
sections.text: Resources in the Imperial Trust are **frozen** except for Imperial Actions (`rule-relative:Campaign Rules & Terms$Resources$Frozen.`).

sections.title: Trophies & Captives
sections.text: **Trophies and Captives** go in the First Regent's Trophies and Captives boxes, respectively. The First Regent does not need to take a Trophy or Captive from themself.

sections.title: Shortfall
sections.text: If a Rival Regent has no pieces shown by the Demand, the First Regent must take 1 agent from the Rival's supply as a **Favor**. If they have ***no agents***, the First Regent may make them an Outlaw.

sections.title: Take Imperial Action
sections.text: After the Imperial Demand, the First Regent must take the **Imperial Action**, as follows:

sections.title: In Peace, Celebrate Regency
sections.text: Each Regent gains the bonus city Power shown on all uncovered city slots on their player board.

sections.title: In Escalation, Requisition Ships
sections.text: Place 2 fresh Imperial ships in an Empire-controlled system. If no systems are controlled by the Empire, place them at a Loyal starport instead.

sections.title: In War, Distribute Arms
sections.text: Give 1 Weapon to each Regent from the supply. If the supply is empty, give it from the Imperial Trust.

sections.title: Guild Envoys Depart
sections.text:
***This card is only used in two-player games.***

Bury all Guild cards in the Court with no agents on them, then refill the Court.

sections.title: Flagships
sections.text: Some Fates give you a Flagship board, piece, and aid card. When you get a Flagship, you also replace all of your Loyal buildings on the map with Free buildings of the same type.

sections.title: Setup
sections.text: Flagship setup is described on the back of the Flagship board. It has been reproduced here for convenience.

sections.title: Step 1: Place Flagship
sections.text: Place a Loyal Flagship piece in a system with Loyal pieces.

sections.title: Step 2: Abandon Buildings
sections.text: Replace all Loyal cities and starports on the map with Free cities and starports, respectively.

sections.title: Step 3: Take Aid Card
sections.text: Take a Flagship Upgrades card.

sections.title: Step 4: Flip Board
sections.text: Flip over the Flagship board and place it below your player board.

sections.title: General Rules
sections.text: Playing a Flagship has some new rules:

sections.title: Fresh Loyal Ship
sections.text: Your Flagship is a fresh Loyal ship that cannot be removed from the map.

sections.title: Building Buildings
sections.text: You cannot **build** Loyal cities or starports on the map. Instead, you can build them on your Flagship board as Upgrades and Armor. (**Upgrades & Armor**, `rule-relative:Flagships$Upgrades & Armor`)

sections.title: Building Ships
sections.text: You can only **build** up to 1 ship at your Flagship per turn, ignoring the number of starports on your Flagship board.

sections.title: Battle with Starports
sections.text: In battle, your Flagship collects a variable number of dice, does not deal hits for  intercept by default, and doesn’t protect buildings on planets. (**Defending**, `rule-relative:Flagships$Flagship Battles$Defending.`)

sections.title: Upgrades & Armor
sections.text:
Your Flagship board has 6 **Upgrade** slots, each with an **Armor** slot above it, that you can build Loyal buildings in.
Upgrades give benefits (`rule-relative:Flagships$Upgrades & Armor$Upgrade Benefits.`). While an Upgrade has Armor, the Upgrade cannot be hit or destroyed.

sections.title: Building
sections.text: To **build** an Upgrade or Armor, your Flagship must be at a planet of the type shown on its slot.

sections.title: Building Armor
sections.text: You can only build Armor if you have its Upgrade and it is fresh.

sections.title: Repairing
sections.text: When you **repair** your Flagship, repair an Upgrade or Armor.

sections.title: Unlike Map Buildings
sections.text: Upgrades and Armor ***do not*** work like buildings on the map:

sections.title: Cannot be Taxed
sections.text: Players cannot **tax** cities on Flagships.

sections.title: Cannot Build or Catapult
sections.text: Players cannot use starports on Flagships to **build** ships or Catapult **move**.

sections.title: Destroying Cities
sections.text: Destroying cities on Flagships does not **Provoke Outrage** or **Ransack the Court**.

sections.title: Cannot be Replaced
sections.text: They cannot be replaced with non-Loyal pieces, such as Free buildings.

sections.title: Upgrade Benefits
sections.text: This section lists the Flagship's Upgrades. The resource types in parentheses are the planet types that your Flagship must be at in order to build the Upgrade and Armor, respectively.

sections.title: Ship Crane
sections.text: You may **build** up to 2 ships per turn in your Flagship's system. Building this upgrade requires your flagship to be at a Material planet, and building this upgrade's armor requires your flagship to be at a Fuel planet.

sections.title: Defense Array
sections.text: When your Flagship is defending in **battle**, it deals intercept hits equal to the number of ***fresh starports*** on its Flagship board. Building this upgrade requires your flagship to be at a **Weapon planet**, and building this upgrade's armor requires your flagship to be at a **Psionic planet**.

sections.title: Slipstream Drive
sections.text: Once per turn, in your Prelude, you may Catapult move either your Flagship alone ***or*** other ships from your Flagship. Building this upgrade requires your flagship to be at a **Fuel planet**, and building this upgrade's armor requires your flagship to be at a **Relic planet**.

sections.title: Control Array
