sections.text: While your Flagship is in a gate, you may **tax** any cities in its cluster like they are Loyal. Building this upgrade requires your flagship to be at a **Psionic planet**, and building this upgrade's armor requires your flagship to be at a **Material planet**.

sections.title: Tractor Beam
sections.text: When your Flagship is defending in **battle**, the attacker cannot collect raid dice. Building this upgrade requires your flagship to be at **a Relic planet**, and building this upgrade's armor requires your flagship to be at **a Weapon planet**.

sections.title: Hull
sections.text: This Upgrade has no unique benefit, but building cities will open resource slots, and building starports will let you collect more dice in battle. You can build this upgrade and its armor when you flagship is at **any planet**.

sections.title: Flagship Battles
sections.text:
There are a few key rules when battling with Flagships:

  - When attacking with a Flagship, its Armor and Upgrades are hit like ***ships***.
  - When defending with a Flagship, its Armor and Upgrades are hit like ***buildings***.

sections.title: Hit Armor First
sections.text: Armor is always hit ***before*** its Upgrade.

sections.title: Collecting Dice
sections.text: When attacking, your Flagship collects dice up to your number of ***fresh starports*** on Upgrades and Armor.

sections.title: Taking Hits as Attacker
sections.text:
While attacking, Upgrades and Armor are hit like ***ships***:
\- You must take hits from `symbol:selfhit` and `symbol:intercept` with Upgrades and Armor if no other attacking ships remain.
\- You can choose to take hits with Upgrades and Armor instead of other attacking ships.

sections.title: Raid Dice Limit
sections.text: While you have a Flagship, Rivals who battle you have a different Raid Dice Limit: they can only collect raid dice if there are ***defending buildings or a defending Flagship***.

sections.title: Does Not Intercept
sections.text: If the attacker rolls a `symbol:intercept`, your Flagship ***does not intercept*** unless it has a Defense Array (`rule-relative:Flagships$Upgrades & Armor$Upgrade Benefits.$Defense Array.`).

sections.title: Taking Hits as Defender
sections.text:
While defending, Upgrades and Armor are hit like ***buildings***:
\- The attacker hits your Upgrades and Armor with `symbol:buildinghit`.
\- If the Flagship is the only remaining defending ship, the attacker hits Upgrades and Armor with `symbol:hit`.
\- Defending buildings on a planet can be hit with `symbol:buildinghit` or with `symbol:hit` if the Flagship is the only remaining defending ship.

sections.title: Taking Hits
sections.text: When taking hits in a Crisis, your Flagship only takes hits if no other fresh Loyal ships remain in the system. Take each hit to your Flagship with your rightmost Armor. If no Armor remains, take the hit with its rightmost Upgrade.

sections.title: Cannot Cede
sections.text: In Summits, you cannot use Cede Control to replace Loyal buildings on your Flagship board with Rival pieces.

sections.title: Cards & Flagships
sections.text: Cards work with Flagships as follows:

sections.title: Building Checks
sections.text: Cards that check for Loyal buildings in a system—like Force Beams, Gate Ports, and Hidden Harbors—count Upgrades and Armor as in your Flagship's system unless the card says “on the map.”

sections.title: Building on the Map
sections.text: Cards that build Loyal buildings outside building slots—like Gate Ports and Cloud Cities—do let you place Loyal buildings on the map again.

sections.title: Ship Improvements
sections.text: Cards that improve your Loyal ships—like Sprinter Drives and Mirror Plating—do improve your Flagship, since it is a fresh Loyal ship.

sections.title: Dice Collection
sections.text: Cards that collect dice for Loyal ships like in battle—like Galactic Rifles—let your Flagship collect 1 die per fresh starport on your Flagship board.

sections.title: Resettling Flagships
sections.text: The “C” Fates let you **Resettle** if you have a Flagship:

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Clear your Flagship board and return it to the box. Replace your Loyal Flagship piece with a Loyal ship.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Place 1 city and 1 starport in empty building slots on the map. If there are none, replace Free buildings.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: If you have fewer than 8 Loyal ships on the map, place ships in systems with Loyal pieces until you have 8 Loyal ships on the map.

sections.title: Intermission
sections.text: The Intermission happens at the end of Act I and Act II. Resolve all of the following steps in order.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Each player resolves the Resolution card in their Fate Set for the current Act. Based on whether you completed or failed your objective, you'll do things like gain or discard cards, add cards to the Court deck, or add cards to the rules booklet.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Each player who failed their objective ***loses Power*** equal to the space of their objective marker on the Power track.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Return all cards in the Court except the Imperial Council to the Court deck.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Return all agents from the Court to their players.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Scrap the Court discard pile.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Return all Trophies and Captives.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Return all frozen resources (`rule-relative:Campaign Rules & Terms$Resources$Frozen.`), including from the Imperial Trust on the First Regent tile, to the supply.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: ***2 Players Only:*** Return all resources from ambition boxes to the supply.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Repair all damaged Blight.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Destroy all damaged ships, buildings, and Flagship Upgrades and Armor.

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: Destroy all buildings in systems that have Blight and no ships.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Give the initiative marker to the player with the ***most Power***.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Each player who has more than 1 Power ***loses half their Power***, rounding to lose less Power.

sections.title: Conceding
sections.text: In games with 2 players, if your Rival has at least ***15 Power*** more than you after halving Power, we recommend that you concede unless you feel confident.

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text:
Each player who completed their objective draws 1 Fate card. Each player who failed it returns their Fate card to the box and draws 2 Fate cards.

  - If you are finishing **Act I**, draw from the **“B” Fates**.
  - If you are finishing **Act II**, draw from the **“C” Fates**.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Each player secretly chooses 1 Fate card from their 2 Fate cards to play in the next Act. Then, everyone reveals their chosen Fate card simultaneously and returns their unchosen Fate card to the box.

sections.title: Switching Fates
sections.text:
If you choose a new Fate card, do the following:
\- Return your current Fate card to the box.
\- Scrap the rest of your Fate Set that is not in play. Don't scrap anything that is in play, including your Flagship if you have one.
\- Return all Favors you have to your Rivals.
\- Take the new Fate Set for your Fate from the box.

sections.title: Next Act?
sections.text: At this point, discuss with everyone whether you want to play the next Act or pack up the game so you can play it later.

sections.title: Next Act
sections.text: If you are playing the next Act, set it up as described in **Act II & III Setup** (`rule:3.2`).

sections.title: Packing Up
sections.text:
If you are packing up, follow these steps. _(Note that you won't be able to play a single-session game of Arcs until you finish the campaign or choose to abandon it!)_

For the next Act, preserve ***everything*** on the map, in the general supply, and in everyone's play areas as follows:

sections.title: Step 1
sections.text: Use a ***log sheet*** to record your names, colors, Fates, Power, Outrage, and Flagship Upgrades and Armor. If a Fate has you record more details, use the blank spaces on the back of the log sheet.

sections.title: Step 2
sections.text: Use the ***2 map trays*** to store the pieces on the map. The trays have sections for each planet (marked with its ID symbol) and each gate (marked “G”).

sections.title: Step 3
sections.text: If a system has too many pieces to fit in the tray, put an ***overflow marker*** in its tray section and put pieces from the system in a bag with the matching overflow marker.

sections.title: Step 4
sections.text: Use the ***4 player trays*** to store the players' play areas. In your tray, use the large well to hold cards in play stacked on top of the cards remaining in your Fate Set. Use the small well to hold everything else in your play area except your player board and Flagship board. You don't need to track the order of your resources.

sections.title: Step 5
sections.text: Keep all of the cards in the ***rules booklet***.

sections.title: Fine Print
sections.text: This section covers some technical parts of play.

sections.title: Tiebreakers
sections.text: If you have a tie and its tiebreaker is not specified, break the tie in turn order. Likewise, if players must make a decision in an unclear order, resolve it in turn order. _(Start with the player with initiative and go clockwise.)_

sections.title: Choice Order
sections.text: If multiple things happen at the same time but must be resolved in order, the player taking their turn chooses their order. If no one is taking a turn, the player with initiative chooses.

sections.title: Elimination
sections.text: Rarely, a player will have no starports or ships on the map. If this happens, they place 3 fresh ships in any gate at the end of their turn.

sections.title: Concession
sections.text: Sometimes, usually in games with 2 players, it may become clear that a player has won. Feel free to concede!

sections.title: Limits
sections.text: Pieces are limited by the contents of the box with one exception: if you need an agent to place on an Outrage slot but none are in your supply, use a placeholder piece until an agent enters your supply, then place the agent.

sections.title: Loyal by Default
sections.text: If a rule makes you **place** pieces, this refers to fresh Loyal pieces by default.

sections.title: Origins
sections.text: Pieces that you **place** and **return** come from and go to their original supply by default except for cities: cities come from the leftmost filled city slot on their original  player board, and go to the rightmost empty city slot. _(Remember, pieces often go to Trophies and Captives instead of back to supplies.)_

sections.title: Do as Much as Possible
sections.text: If you must **place** or **return** more pieces than possible, do the maximum possible.

sections.title: Replace
sections.text: If you **replace** a piece, return it and place another piece in its place. If the old piece was damaged, the new piece is placed damaged. _(Replacing a piece does not destroy it.)_

sections.title: Rulebook
sections.text: This rulebook supersedes the aid sheets and player boards.

sections.title: Cards
sections.text: Cards supersede this rulebook, but any rule that uses the term **cannot** is absolute—it cannot be superseded unless explicitly named using the term **ignore**. _(For example, “You ignore Outrage when spending Material for its Prelude action.”)_

sections.title: Clarifications
sections.text: Sidebars as well as text written in italics and parentheses _(like this)_ are clarifications and reminders, which are superseded by the core rules they reference.

sections.title: Agreements
sections.text: Players may make deals and promises, but they are not binding.

sections.title: Transfer of Pieces
sections.text: Players cannot give each other pieces unless a rule allows it.

sections.title: Hands
sections.text: Players cannot show the action cards in their hand to anyone else.

sections.title: Sequencing
sections.text: Though declaring an ambition and seizing the initiative happen before any other actions, we usually let people do them during their turn as long as new info hasn't been revealed—such as rolling dice or drawing a card—and any relevant modifiers are followed. Don't get bogged down in technicalities unless it changes the game. _Arcs_ thrives when the game flows!

sections.title: Split Discard Piles
sections.text: Normally, all action cards are discarded face down, even ones played face up. This speeds up play but it favors players with good memory. If you're running a tournament or want a more strategic but slower game, you can split the action discard into two piles — one for cards played face down, and one for cards played face up.

sections.title: Drawing
sections.text: If you're prompted to draw from the action discard pile, draw from the facedown pile. In the rare circumstance that it doesn't have enough cards, shuffle the piles together first.

sections.title: Adjacent
sections.text: Shares a thin border (**The Map**, `rule-relative:Core Concepts$The Map$Adjacency.`).

sections.title: Building
sections.text: Cities and starports.

sections.title: Bury
sections.text: Place on the bottom of the Court deck.

sections.title: Capture
sections.text: Place the prompted piece in the Captives box on your player board.

sections.title: Chapter
sections.text: The time in which players play rounds until they all run out of action cards.

sections.title: Clear
sections.text: Return all pieces from the prompted area.

sections.title: Control
sections.text: You control a system and its contents if you have more fresh ships there than each Rival. On a tie, no one controls the system.

sections.title: Damaged
sections.text: Not ***fresh***—a tipped ship or a building on its darker side.

sections.title: Destroy
sections.text: Return a fresh or damaged piece from the map. _(It often goes to a Trophies box.)_

sections.title: Empty
sections.text: Has no pieces in or on it.

sections.title: Fresh
sections.text: Not ***damaged***—an upright ship or a building on its lighter side.

sections.title: Gain
sections.text: Add the specified piece to your play area ***from its supply***. _(You can't gain it if its supply is empty.)_

sections.title: Give
sections.text: Add the specified piece to a Rival play area.

sections.title: Hit
sections.text: Tip over a fresh piece on the map, or remove a damaged piece from the map.

sections.title: Loyal
sections.text: Of your player color.

sections.title: Out of Play
sections.text: Cannot be interacted with.

sections.title: Piece
sections.text: Any component in the game.

sections.title: Place
sections.text: See **Pieces & Piece Limits** (`rule-relative:Fine Print$Pieces & Piece Limits`).

sections.title: Play Area
sections.text: On and around your player board. _(Most pieces go in specific parts of your play area.)_

sections.title: Prelude
sections.text: See **Prelude Actions** (`rule-relative:Other Actions$Prelude Actions`).

sections.title: Replace, Return
sections.text: See **Pieces & Piece Limits** (`rule-relative:Fine Print$Pieces & Piece Limits`).

sections.title: Rival
sections.text: Of another player's color. When used alone, refers to another player.

sections.title: Round
sections.text: The time in which each player takes a turn.

sections.title: Scrap
sections.text: Make ***out of play*** permanently.

sections.title: Seize the Initiative
sections.text: Take the initiative marker. You cannot do this if you have the initiative marker or if someone has already seized the initiative this round.

sections.title: Spend
sections.text: When referring to a resource, return the spent resource to its supply.

sections.title: Steal
sections.text: Add the specified piece to your play area ***from a Rival's play area***. _(This is distinct from ***take*** because some rules prevent stealing.)_

sections.title: Supply
sections.text: The general supply holds resources and other shared pieces, and players' supplies hold their Loyal ships and agents.

sections.title: Swap
sections.text: Give the prompted piece and take the prompted piece at the same time.

sections.title: Take
sections.text: Add the specified piece to your play area.

sections.title: Turn
sections.text: The time in which a player plays an action card and may take actions.

sections.title: Turn Order
sections.text: Starting with the player with initiative and going clockwise.

Edited to: "Discard all action cards not in players' hands into a facedown action discard pile on the map, **then shuffle it**."
*There are a couple situations where discard order matters.*
This text was added to clarify when leader setup happens.

Edited to: "Discard all action cards not in players' hands into the action discard pile on the map face down, **then shuffle it**."
*There are a couple situations where discard order matters.*

Edited to: "Some cards say they hold resources. These resources can be spent and add to ambitions, **but they cannot be stolen in battle unless explicitly allowed.** If a card holding resources is stolen, the resources on the card stay on it. If it is buried, discarded, **or scrapped,** the resources on it return to the supply."
*(NOT YET IN PRINT) This clarifies some card interactions with raiding, Blighted Reach cards, and with cards like Silver-Tongues. Yes, you can steal resources off cards with Silver-Tongues!*
Edited "Imperial ships" to "Imperial **pieces**" to better support interactions with Fates.

These rules have been expanded to allow more card types than lore to interact with Flagships in the same way. For example, this allows edicts like [Policy of Escalation](https://cards.buriedgiantstudios.com/card/ARCS-AID05) to interact with Flagships.

Added "This counts as stealing."
*This clarifies interactions with cards like [Pirate Hoard](https://cards.buriedgiantstudios.com/card/ARCS-F1202).*

Edited to "Resources in the Imperial Trust are frozen **except for Imperial Actions**."
*The Distribute Arms action under Imperial Actions already states that you give the Weapon from the Imperial Trust, but this addition codifies the exception for clarity.*

This rule now explicitly states, rather than implies, that cards like [Command Chaos](https://cards.buriedgiantstudios.com/card/ARCS-F713) can remove Imperial Officers, even though it’s protected, because it states it by name.
This rule now explicitly states, rather than implies, that **scrap** can target frozen resources.

On page 2 in the first printing, in the Stop box, mentions of "deep wells" should say "lower wells."
*The deep well is where the removable trays are stored, not the small cards.*
This is now clarified so that the limitation applies regardless of who played or secured something, unless the Council is no longer happening at the end of the round.

Added "If it flips while tucked under a card, return it to the Court."
*After some soul-searching, we have reversed the previous behavior of the Council. This means cards like [Council Intrigue](https://cards.buriedgiantstudios.com/card/ARCS-CC12) can flip the Council while it’s tucked under a card in the card play area, returning it to the Court. This means the Council won't resolve at the end of the round!*

Edited "To do this" to "At this time" to clarify that you can always rearrange when you take a resource.
